questions.q: Which picture is closest to a data lake?
options: A library where every book is catalogued before it is shelved
A tidy desk where nothing gets in without a label
A big storage room where everything goes in as it arrives
A single shelf that belongs to one department
questions.explain: A lake keeps data exactly as it arrives, in any format. Nobody has to decide up front what each item is for. The library and the tidy desk are the warehouse, and the department shelf is a data mart.

questions.q: A shop saves its raw website click logs now and works out the columns later, when an analyst asks a question. Which idea is that?
options: Structure applied before storing, as in a warehouse
Structure applied when you read the data, as in a lake
A data mart for the marketing team
A report that is already cleaned and checked
questions.explain: Store now, decide later. That is a lake applying structure when you read (schema-on-read). A warehouse does the opposite and shapes the data before it is stored.

questions.q: Your finance team needs numbers that must match exactly, every time. Where should that data live first?
options: A lake, so nothing gets changed on the way in
A lake, because it is cheaper to store
Neither, because exact numbers are not possible
A warehouse, because the data is cleaned and checked on the way in
questions.explain: Warehouses are more reliable because de-duplication and verification happen in advance. That is why the post's map points trusted, exact numbers to a warehouse.

questions.q: How do many large organisations use lakes and warehouses together?
options: Data lands in a lake first, then clean subsets load into warehouses and marts
They pick one and delete the other
Data skips the lake and goes straight into marts
They copy the whole warehouse back into the lake every night
questions.explain: So you rarely have to choose. The lake keeps the raw copy, and the warehouse serves the trusted reports.

questions.q: What can happen to a data lake that nobody looks after?
options: It quietly turns into a faster warehouse
It can turn into a data swamp, full of data nobody trusts
It removes its own duplicates
It shrinks into a data mart
questions.explain: Without a management layer, lakes can become messy mires where good data is hard to find. A lake needs owners, names and rules to stay useful.
